html:
SMTO-AUT-0012 — SMTO couldn't confirm the sign-in response was genuine

GUID: 81679319-ace5-5780-9d37-de153c1e996d
Slug: auth-invalid-state
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: auth-broker

What happened

  • After you signed in, the reply from the service didn't match the sign-in SMTO started, so SMTO refused it to avoid connecting the wrong account. This often happens with reused or old sign-in pages.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close the sign-in tab, return to SMTO, and ask SMTO in the conversation to try the step again so it shows a new Open authorization page link. Each reply from the service can be used only once and must match the sign-in SMTO just started.
  2. Always open SMTO at the same address, the one this connection was set up with, and don't refresh or bookmark the page the service sends you back to. SMTO rejects replies that come back to a different address or are repeated from an earlier sign-in.
  3. Don't restart SMTO while a sign-in is in progress. SMTO keeps unfinished sign-ins only in memory, so after a restart it can't recognize the reply.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in page says Authorization complete, and the Task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection; they may need to check its sign-in settings. Don't share the address of the page the service sent you back to, because it can contain a one-time code.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth callback failed validation: unknown or already-used state, redirect URI mismatch, missing or wrong issuer, a missing or invalid authorization code, or an ID token that failed signature, issuer, audience or nonce checks.

What this means

  • Callback state, issuer, required identity token or signed identity claims failed validation against the registered client and pending transaction. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • Callback state, issuer, required identity token or signed identity claims failed validation against the registered client and pending transaction.

How to diagnose it

  • Check registered callback, issuer and identity-validation stage; preserve private codes and tokens outside diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Verify that the oauth2_client issuer matches the provider's discovery document, that redirect_uri exactly equals the address SMTO is reached at followed by /api/agent/auth/oauth/callback, and that jwks_uri and id_token_algorithms allow the ID token to be verified. Then begin a new authorization; callbacks are single-use and pending transactions are lost when the Server restarts.
  • Verify issuer, registered callback and trusted signing configuration, then begin a new authorization. Do not reuse the callback.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the reported condition and check delivery evidence before starting another operation.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh callback passes state, issuer and signed-identity validation for the intended client.

What not to do

  • Do not expose passwords, access tokens, authorization codes or SMTP authentication payloads.
  • Do not automatically repeat an operation whose remote effect is unknown.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
